main_issue: Who completes Agent D's half-finished analysis section before Thursday's pitch, given D's bereavement (D working from home vs. B/C taking it vs. A taking it)

A-B.evidence: A asks B to take over (T5); B declines (T6); B never takes a position on A's later plan, so the relation stays unclear.

A-C.evidence: A pushes C to take the section (T7, T12, T15), and C refuses (T8, T14, T16); A then gives in: 'I'll take over the analysis' (T18), which resolves C's objection.

A-D.evidence: D insists on working from home (T9, T11, T17) and A refuses (T10, T18); D finally agrees: 'Okay. Yes. I can do that. Thank you' (T21), then walks A through the work (T31).

B-C.evidence: Both decline to take on D's section (T6, T8), but neither speaks to the other and B says nothing after that.

B-D.evidence: B offers condolences and declines to take the work (T6); B takes no position on D's offer to work from home or the final arrangement.

C-D.evidence: D concedes that 'Agent C has a point' about the analysis (T17), then accepts A's plan, which takes the burden off C (T21).
